title: What are Promises?
overview: A Promise is a JavaScript object that represents the result of an asynchronous operation. It can handle operations that complete successfully or fail in the future.

example.title: Promise Example

title: Promise States
overview: A Promise has three states: pending, fulfilled, and rejected. These states represent the current status of an asynchronous operation.

example.title: Promise States
example.content:
Pending:
Operation is running.

Fulfilled:
Operation completed successfully.

Rejected:
Operation failed.

title: Creating a Promise
overview: Promises are created using the Promise constructor. It receives a function with resolve and reject parameters to handle success and failure.

example.title: Create Promise

title: then and catch Methods
overview: The then method handles successful Promise results, while the catch method handles errors when a Promise is rejected.

title: Promise Chaining
overview: Promise chaining allows multiple asynchronous operations to be executed one after another by connecting multiple then methods.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned what promises are, their states, how to create promises, handle results using then and catch, and perform multiple asynchronous operations using chaining.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:

✔ then handles success.
